title_en: Zhunge'erqi Dingfeng Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd. v. China Railway Tenth Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over jurisdiction objection concerning railway construction contract
ruling_gist_en: When determining the level of jurisdiction for cases under the exclusive jurisdiction of railway transport courts, a case where one party's domicile is within the jurisdiction of the railway transport court and the other party's domicile is neither within the jurisdiction of the railway transport court nor within the administrative jurisdiction of the province where the railway transport court is located falls under the category of 'a case where one party's domicile is not within the jurisdiction of the provincial high people's court.' That is, the jurisdiction of the railway transport court is also part of the jurisdiction of the provincial high people's court to which it belongs.

full_text_en:
Jungar Banner Dingfeng Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd. v. China Railway Tenth Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over jurisdiction of railway construction contract

Ruling Summary

When determining the level of jurisdiction for a case that falls within the exclusive jurisdiction of a railway transport court, if one party's domicile is within the jurisdiction of the railway transport court, and the other party's domicile is neither within the jurisdiction of the railway transport court nor within the administrative jurisdiction of the province where the railway transport court is located, the case is considered one where "the domicile of one party is not within the jurisdiction of the High People's Court of the province." That is to say, the jurisdiction of the railway transport court is also within the jurisdiction of the High People's Court of the province to which it belongs.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Ruling

(2013) Min Ti Zi No. 231

Reapplicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): China Railway Tenth Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Building 7, Shuntai Plaza, No. 2000 Shunhua Road, Gaoxin District, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Shen Yaoxing, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Sun Jianping, Head of the Legal Affairs Department of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Song Guilin, General Legal Counsel of the Company.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Jungar Banner Dingfeng Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd., domiciled at Kaiyuan Road, Xuejiawan Town, Jungar Banner, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: He Yutao, Chairman of the Board.

The Reapplicant, China Railway Tenth Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as China Railway Tenth), filed an application for retrial with this Court, challenging the civil ruling (2013) Jin Li Shang Zhong Zi No. 14 rendered by the Shanxi High People's Court in a dispute over jurisdiction regarding a railway construction contract with the Respondent, Jungar Banner Dingfeng Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dingfeng Company). This Court issued the civil ruling (2013) Min Shen Zi No. 1783, granting the retrial and bringing the case up for trial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and conducted a hearing. The case is now concluded.

On April 16, 2013, Dingfeng Company filed a lawsuit against China Railway Tenth with the Taiyuan Railway Transport Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Taiyuan Railway Intermediate Court) concerning a dispute over a railway construction contract, requesting: First, an order that China Railway Tenth repay Dingfeng Company the overpaid project funds in the amount of RMB 64,800,276.86; Second, an order that China Railway Tenth pay Dingfeng Company liquidated damages of RMB 18,000,000.00; Third, an order that China Railway Tenth pay liquidated damages for overdue payment; Fourth, an order that China Railway Tenth issue a project invoice for RMB 16,000,000; Fifth, an order that China Railway Tenth bear all litigation costs in this case. After the expiration of the response period, China Railway Tenth raised a jurisdictional objection with the court of first instance, contending: First, the subject matter of this lawsuit amounts to over RMB 80,000,000, and the domicile of China Railway Tenth is not within the jurisdiction of Shanxi Province. Therefore, under the law, this is a first-instance civil case within the jurisdiction of the Shanxi High People's Court, and the Taiyuan Railway Intermediate Court has no jurisdiction over this case. Second, based on the jurisdictional agreement in the "Construction Contract" involved, no single court with jurisdiction can be determined, so the jurisdictional agreement is unclear and invalid. This case should be subject to the general principles of territorial jurisdiction, and should be heard by the court at the defendant's domicile or the place of contract performance. The request is to transfer the case to the Shandong High People's Court, which has jurisdiction over the defendant's domicile.

The Taiyuan Railway Intermediate Court held at first instance: China Railway Tenth did not raise a jurisdictional objection within the statutory period, and even applied to the court for investigation and evidence collection and for an extension of the evidence submission period. This should be deemed as its acknowledgment that the court has jurisdiction. The project involved in this case is an ancillary facility of the national railway Shuozhou-Huaihua line. According to Article 3, Paragraph 6, of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on the Jurisdiction of Railway Transport Courts, this case should be under the exclusive jurisdiction of a railway transport court. The construction site of this project (the place of contract performance) is within the business jurisdiction of the Taiyuan Railway Bureau. Both parties set up offices at the construction site, and the project management department of China Railway Tenth for the Jungar Banner Coal Collection and Transportation Station Railway Special Line was registered with the local Jungar Banner Railway Project Management Office. Accordingly, both the plaintiff and the defendant should be deemed to be within the same jurisdiction of the railway court. Pursuant to the Jin Gao Fa [2008] No. 5 document issued by the Shanxi High People's Court, this court may accept first-instance cases with a subject matter below RMB 100,000,000. Therefore, the Taiyuan Railway Intermediate Court has jurisdiction over this case and does not violate the rules on subject-matter or territorial jurisdiction. China Railway Tenth's argument that its domicile and the place of contract performance are not within the jurisdiction of the Taiyuan Railway Intermediate Court is incorrect, and the court does not support it. Ruling: The jurisdictional objection raised by China Railway Tenth in this case is dismissed.

China Railway Tenth, dissatisfied with the first-instance ruling, appealed to the Shanxi High People's Court. The Shanxi High People's Court held at second instance: The "Construction Contract" signed by both parties on October 9, 2011, stipulated that disputes would be resolved by "filing a lawsuit with a competent court at the project location." This case concerns a dispute over a construction contract for a railway special line. The project location, which is also the place of contract performance, is within the jurisdiction of the Taiyuan Railway Bureau. According to Article 3, Paragraph 6, of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on the Jurisdiction of Railway Transport Courts, this case falls under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Taiyuan Railway Transport Intermediate Court. Neither party in this case is within the jurisdiction of Shanxi Province. Pursuant to the Supreme People's Court's Standards for the Jurisdiction of First-Instance Civil and Commercial Cases by High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts of Various Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly Under the Central Government, the Taiyuan Railway Intermediate Court has jurisdiction over cases with a subject matter of RMB 5,000,000 or more but less than RMB 100,000,000. Therefore, the court of first instance correctly held that it has jurisdiction over this case, and the ruling should be affirmed. The appellant's grounds for appeal are not sustainable and are not supported. Ruling: The appeal is dismissed, and the original ruling is affirmed.

China Railway Tenth applied for retrial, contending: First, according to the Supreme People's Court's Standards for the Jurisdiction of First-Instance Civil and Commercial Cases by High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts of Various Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly Under the Central Government, the Shanxi High People's Court has jurisdiction over first-instance civil and commercial cases with a subject matter of RMB 100,000,000 or more, as well as first-instance civil and commercial cases with a subject matter of RMB 50,000,000 or more where the domicile of one party is not within its jurisdiction, or which involve foreign, Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan elements. This case is one where "one party is not within this jurisdiction," and the subject matter of the lawsuit amounts to over RMB 80,000,000. Therefore, the first instance should be under the jurisdiction of a high people's court, and the Taiyuan Railway Transport Intermediate Court has no jurisdiction over this case. Second, the "Construction Contract" signed by both parties stipulates that "disputes shall be resolved by a competent court at the project location." The project location, Jungar Banner, is administratively under the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, while its railway management falls under the Taiyuan Railway Bureau. Given the subject matter of this case and the domiciles of the parties, the first instance should be under the jurisdiction of a high people's court. According to the parties' agreement, both the Shanxi High People's Court and the Inner Mongolia High People's Court would have jurisdiction, making it impossible to determine a single court with jurisdiction. Therefore, the agreement is unclear and invalid. This case should be governed by Article 23 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and be heard by a court at the defendant's domicile or the place of contract performance. The request is to transfer the case to the Shandong High People's Court, which has jurisdiction over the defendant's domicile.

The Respondent, Dingfeng Company, did not submit a written defense.

This Court finds upon trial: Article 1 of the "Construction Contract" signed by Dingfeng Company and China Railway Tenth on October 9, 2011, stipulates: "The project location is the south side of Narisong Town, Jungar Banner, Ordos City." Article 35 stipulates: "If no agreement is reached through mediation, a lawsuit shall be filed with a competent court at the project location."

This Court holds: The parties agreed in the "Construction Contract" signed by both parties that "if no agreement is reached through mediation, a lawsuit shall be filed with a competent court at the project location." This agreement represents the true intent of both parties, and the designated "court at the project location" is clear. It complies with Article 34 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 24 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and thus should be deemed valid. This case concerns a dispute over a construction contract for a railway special line. Pursuant to Article 3, Paragraph 6, of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on the Jurisdiction of Railway Transport Courts, which provides that "contract disputes related to the construction of railways and their ancillary facilities" shall be under the jurisdiction of railway transport courts, this case should be under the exclusive jurisdiction of a railway transport court. The project location, Jungar Banner, is within the jurisdiction of the Taiyuan Railway Bureau and falls within the jurisdiction of the Taiyuan Railway Transport Intermediate Court. The domicile of the plaintiff at first instance, Dingfeng Company, is in Jungar Banner, which is within the jurisdiction of the Taiyuan Railway Transport Intermediate Court and therefore also within the jurisdiction of the Shanxi High People's Court. The domicile of the defendant at first instance, China Railway Tenth, is in Jinan City, Shandong Province, which is neither within the jurisdiction of the Taiyuan Railway Bureau nor within the jurisdiction of Shanxi Province, and thus is not within the jurisdiction of the Shanxi High People's Court. According to the Supreme People's Court's Standards for the Jurisdiction of First-Instance Civil and Commercial Cases by High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts of Various Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly Under the Central Government, the Shanxi High People's Court has jurisdiction over first-instance civil and commercial cases with a subject matter of RMB 100,000,000 or more, as well as first-instance civil and commercial cases with a subject matter of RMB 50,000,000 or more where the domicile of one party is not within its jurisdiction. The subject matter of this case is over RMB 80,000,000, and the domicile of the defendant at first instance, China Railway Tenth, is not within the jurisdiction of the Shanxi High People's Court. Therefore, this case falls under the jurisdiction of the Shanxi High People's Court as a first-instance civil case, and the Taiyuan Railway Transport Intermediate Court has no jurisdiction over this case. The findings of the first and second instance rulings that the Taiyuan Railway Transport Intermediate Court has jurisdiction over this case are improper.

In conclusion, the first and second instance rulings incorrectly applied the law, and China Railway Tenth's argument that this case should be under the jurisdiction of a High People's Court is well-founded. Pursuant to Article 200, Paragraph 6, and Article 207, Paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court rules as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2013) Tai Tie Zhong Shang Chu Zi No. 4 of the Taiyuan Railway Transport Intermediate People's Court and the civil ruling (2013) Jin Li Shang Zhong Zi No. 14 of the Shanxi High People's Court are hereby reversed.

2. The Shanxi High People's Court shall hear this case as the court of first instance.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Zhang Zhihong
Acting Judge: Li Zhenhua
Acting Judge: Jia Yaqi

November 26, 2013
